schools.note: Small-group surf lessons at Bantham since May 2025, alongside its Bigbury base. Group lessons from age 6 for confident swimmers; one-to-one from age 4.

schools.note: Beginner, kids', improver, private and bodyboarding lessons, plus SUP lessons and tours and a kids' surf club. Picks the best spot each day.

lessonsIntro: Bantham is South Devon's best-known surf beach, and lessons run from the beach car park in season. Coaches will tell you which part of the beach is safest on the day.

text: Bantham picks up more Atlantic swell than most South Devon beaches, and it's widely seen as the most consistent break on this coast. The beach break here is friendly enough for beginners, and the shallow water suits families. Discovery Surf School meets learners at its van in the beach car park and keeps groups small, and staff will advise on the best time and part of the beach to go in.

The big hazard is the River Avon, which meets the sea at Bantham. It creates fast rip currents and the strongest currents in the bay, especially when the river is running hard. The river mouth wave is usually surfed around low tide and is best left to experienced surfers. RNLI lifeguards patrol daily from early May to late September, so learn between the flags and away from the river.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Beginners with care
cards.text: A beginner-friendly beach break, but the river mouth is for experienced surfers only.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: May to September
cards.text: RNLI lifeguards patrol daily from 2 May to 27 September 2026, 10am to 6pm.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: River Avon rips
cards.text: Fast rip currents at the river mouth, strongest when the river is running quickly.

hireIntro: You can hire boards and wetsuits from the Bantham car park, and there's a surf shop with hire a couple of miles inland.

text: Learn on a big soft board in the white water, then move to a mid-length once you're catching green waves. Bodyboarding is popular here, but keep it between the red and yellow flags. The sea here runs from about 15-19C in mid-August to 9-10C in early March. A 3/2mm or 4/3mm suits summer; in colder months Discovery Surf School puts everyone in a 5mm suit, with boots, gloves and a hood available.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Soft-top to mid-length
cards.text: Soft boards for beginners; 6ft to 9ft boards are available for improvers.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 3/2 summer, 5mm winter
cards.text: A 3/2mm or 4/3mm in summer; a 5mm suit with boots, gloves and a hood in the colder months.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Bodyboards, SUP and kayak
cards.text: Bodyboard between the flags. SUPs and kayaks are hired here too, but stay clear of surfers and the river current.

shopsIntro: There's no surf shop on the beach itself, but a full surf shop sits about two miles away near Kingsbridge.
shopsText: There's no surf shop on the beach at Bantham. Triocean Surf, about two miles away at Churchstow near Kingsbridge, sells wetsuits, surfboards, bodyboards and paddleboards, and its workshop repairs boards and wetsuits. Across the river at Bigbury-on-Sea, Discovery Surf School has a small shop for hoodies and changing robes.

lessons.a: Discovery Surf School meets you at its van in the Bantham beach car park (TQ7 3AN). Arrive 20 minutes early to change.
Discovery takes children from 6 in group lessons if they can swim 50m confidently, and from 4 in one-to-one lessons.

lessons.q: Is the river mouth safe for beginners?
lessons.a: No. The River Avon creates fast rips there. Learn in the main beach break between the lifeguard flags.

hire.q: What can I hire at Bantham?
hire.a: Surfboards, wetsuits, bodyboards, SUPs and kayaks, from the car park or from Triocean Surf's hire.

hire.q: What do I need to leave as a deposit?
hire.a: Discovery Surf School prefers photo ID, such as a driving licence.

shops.q: Where can I get a board repaired near Bantham?
shops.a: Triocean Surf's workshop, about two miles from the beach, repairs surfboards, SUPs and wetsuits.
